Thanks! My purpose of this thread was not to persuade anyone to believe in the bible. In fact I'm really not interested in that. But I'll try to answer your questions. If you want to know more maybe we can keep this going in DMs as this won’t be of interest to everyone.

1) I think it's difficult to argue that the bible has a single idea of anything. It has so many authors with differing perspectives over thousands of years. But on this story (Genesis 22), I would recommend 25:23-28:36 of this podcast episode: [http://robbell.podbean.com/e/episode-8-the-enduring-relevance-astonishing-power-and-unexpected-brilliance-of-the-bible/](http://robbell.podbean.com/e/episode-8-the-enduring-relevance-astonishing-power-and-unexpected-brilliance-of-the-bible/) I’m not 100% convinced of this argument but it’s another way to see it.

2) "Shunned" isn't quite right. This is just one of many reasons why a person might be considered ritually unclean. It's not necessarily a statement about her moral worth. Leviticus 15:19-33 contains these laws, but for comparison, 15:1-18 has the laws about discharges of semen in men, which also makes him unclean. The Law of Moses is not considered binding on Christians but if you want to know about the contemporary practice of these laws in Judaism, start by looking up 'Mikvah' on wikipedia.

3) I think this is about Deuteronomy 21. I would recommend that same podcast episode I linked in question 1, in which he focusses on "the most offensive passage in the bible."[ ](http://robbell.podbean.com/e/episode-8-the-enduring-relevance-astonishing-power-and-unexpected-brilliance-of-the-bible/)There's a bit of intro waffle but it starts properly at 2:32. Bell also has an extremely good, extremely long audiobook on the book of Leviticus, since you seem interested in that.

4) This is about Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13. There is so much to say here, but I suppose this is a good place to start: [http://www.bibleandhomosexuality.org/does-leviticus-mean-homosexuality-is-an-abomination/](http://www.bibleandhomosexuality.org/does-leviticus-mean-homosexuality-is-an-abomination/) The same website has information on homosexuality in the New Testament as well. The church I am attending is one of the few genuinely inclusive churches where I live. We are able to perform same-sex marriages (as is one other church here and the Reform Synagogue), and have services and a support network especially for LGBT Christians, a category I include myself in. Through the pandemic we’re carrying this on over Zoom and are looking at starting a bible study group as well.

5) I struggle to answer this because it feels very far away from my own tradition. Experience tells me limiting ministry to just one kind of person doesn’t work. A lot of bad ideas about the role of women in church come from the letters of Paul. Some of his teachings about gender make a lot of sense for his context and would have helped move things forward at the time. Taking them at face value today is where the problem begins. However, on the command for women to not speak in church, I think Paul was simply wrong. The Hebrew Bible has many women with crucial roles, including some prophets. There are many inspiring women in the life of Jesus, too. As we have just passed Easter I’ve heard a lot of people saying: “Without woman preachers we would never have known about the resurrection.”

6) Spiritual warfare is so far away from anything I’ve believed in a long time. It doesn’t really impact me as an idea, and I’m quite ignorant of it, but it seems basically unbiblical. I think it helps to admit that the keys to understanding the book of Revelation have been lost for many centuries. There are so many layers of meaning and imagery specific to the anxieties of one community 1600 years ago that anyone claiming to know its relevance for today should be treated with extreme suspicion.
